description:
🌌 The Void Walkers

We are The Void Walkers, a team of curious minds passionate about space, science, technology, and innovation. Our goal is to explore real-world challenges using creativity, teamwork, and technology to build impactful solutions with NASA's open data.

We welcome enthusiastic people skilled in Coding, Software Development, AI/ML, Data Analysis, Earth & Space Science. If you love exploring the unknown and turning ideas into reality, join us on this journey beyond the ordinary!
summary: Marswalk Navigator is a web map that gives a future Mars astronaut one layered view of the ground they plan to walk on. It combines NASA Mars photos, thermal and elevation layers with USGS terrain models, a route preview that shows distance, elevation and slope, the geologic unit at a point, and Perseverance sample sites and rover photos. It answers the “Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map” challenge by bringing global and regional NASA data down to the scale of a single Marswalk. It matters because crews will need terrain, geology and surface context in one place to plan routes safely and do science along the way.
details:
What it does. Marswalk Navigator is an interactive map of Mars. Users can switch between NASA layers, pick a Perseverance sample site (Malay or Ha’ahóni) or two points, and preview a route. For the route it shows distance, an elevation profile and slope where terrain data exists. Selecting a point shows the geologic unit and whether USGS terrain models cover it. A “What to expect” panel shows sample Perseverance rover photos, with links to NASA’s official gallery.

How it works. The map uses Mars Trek tiles in the Mars equirectangular projection. Terrain models come from a USGS catalog and are read from cloud-optimized GeoTIFFs in the browser. The geologic unit comes from the USGS Geologic Map of Mars service.

Benefits. Crew and planners see photos, thermal, elevation, terrain and geology together, at the small scale of a single walk.

Limits. This is a planning preview, not a safety rating. Slope is averaged over about 200 m, terrain models cover only part of Mars, the route is a straight preview line (up to 500 km) and the geologic map is regional. The rover photos shown are samples and are not tied to the selected route.

Goal. A simple, honest starting point for hazard-aware Mars route planning.

Tools. React, Vite, OpenLayers, geotiff.js, proj4 JavaScript. alos used AI assistance from OpenAI Codex and Anthropic’s Claude.
